name: Destiny Mastercard
perks: Unsecured card with no security deposit required
$700 credit limit on the current standard offer, higher than many subprime cards
Prequalification uses a soft pull that does not affect your score
Reports to all three major credit bureaus (Equifax, Experian, TransUnion)
drawbacks: Annual fee is $175 the first year, then $49 plus $12.50 per month (about $199 per year) after that, as of mid-2026; terms vary by offer
Fee math: the $175 first-year fee eats 25% of a $700 limit the day the card opens, and the ongoing fees keep charging you roughly $199 a year for the privilege of a $700 line
35.9% purchase APR, among the highest of any mainstream card
No rewards, no cash back, and no reliable path to credit limit increases or an upgrade
Issued by First Electronic Bank and serviced by Concora Credit, the same servicer behind the Indigo card, with a similar complaint record on fees and servicing
Over three years you would pay roughly $573 in fees; a Discover it Secured or Capital One Platinum Secured costs $0 in fees over the same period and gives your deposit back
Verdict: not recommended; nearly anyone approved for Destiny can either fund a small secured deposit or get approved for Mission Lane, and both are cheaper ways to rebuild
